thread.title: What high CEO salaries can do to worker productivity

author: Maria LaMagna
title: What high CEO salaries can do to worker productivity
text:
Some employees really don’t like how much their CEOs get paid — and that can affect the company’s performance.
It’s common for chief executives to make significantly higher salaries than lower-level employees do, but that disparity can actually hurt companies , according to a new working paper by Ethan Rouen, an assistant professor at Harvard Business School. When a CEO is “overpaid” and employees are “underpaid,” the firm performance suffers the most, he said.
Those companies saw high levels of turnover, as well as lower sales and dissatisfied employees. Rather than motivating employees, the high CEO salaries seemed to weigh down workers and their aspirations. “If you’re not making your employees happy and creating an environment where they’re doing their best work, your firm is not going to succeed,” Rouen said.
Rouen analyzed U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data for 931 firms in the S&P 1500, between 2006 and 2013. He decided to do the study after the Securities and Exchange Commission implemented a rule that will require companies to disclose the ratio of the CEO’s compensation to median employee pay starting in 2018. 
The average salary for the CEOs of those companies was $5.8 million per year, and the average employee earned $42,000 per year. Rouen created ratios of CEO pay to employee pay for each company, while also taking into account economic factors that could influence how much each are paid, including worker performance and labor market characteristics.
In cases where a CEO’s high pay couldn’t be explained by economic factors, he called that an “unexplained pay ratio.” He found that companies with a high unexplained pay ratio showed worse performances than industry competitors that didn’t have such high ratios. Though the SEC’s new rule about disclosing CEO compensation ratios is designed to address inflated CEO pay.
The average CEO of an S&P 500 company makes approximately 347 times more money than the average worker, according to data released last year by Executive Pay Watch, a report conducted by the American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations. CEOs were paid 335 times the average worker who’ve seen their pay rise 3% per year. 
How much he boss is paid is a hard subject to avoid. Apple AAPL, +0.09% and Amazon AMZN, -0.13% for instance, obviously employ retail and warehouse workers who make comparatively low salaries. Apple disclosed in late December that CEO Tim Cook made $12.8 million in 2017. Apple strives for a familial, if sometimes secretive and fiercely loyal, corporate culture. Amazon CEO, meanwhile, is one of the richest men in the world.
A study from researchers at Singapore Management University, the University of Maryland and Oakland University came to a different conclusion than Rouen’s. It found that a small increase in CEO pay ratio could actually be tied to stronger company performance . They attributed that to the idea that higher pay allows firms to hire better-performing CEOs.
